_meta.indication: Gadolinium-based contrast agent indicated for use in magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) to evaluate aortoiliac occlusive disease (AIOD) in adults with known or suspected peripheral vascular disease

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Two Phase 3 aortoiliac MRA studies, MS-325-12 and MS-325-13 (combined/re-read for approval)
pivotal_trials.design: Two multi-center, open-label, single-arm (blinded-read) Phase 3 trials; patients underwent MRA with and without VASOVIST and catheter-based X-ray arteriography as the reference standard
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with known or suspected peripheral vascular disease evaluated for aortoiliac occlusive disease; median age 67 years (range 29 to 87), 83% white, 68% male
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Superiority in sensitivity and non-inferiority in specificity of VASOVIST-MRA versus non-contrast MRA at the vessel-segment level for detecting occlusive disease (>=50% stenosis)
pivotal_trials.n: 493 patients enrolled across the two trials; 424 included in the diagnostic efficacy comparison
pivotal_trials.result: Superiority in sensitivity and non-inferiority in specificity demonstrated by all three readers; sensitivity differences VASOVIST-MRA vs non-contrast: 20% (95% CI 15%, 25%), 12% (7%, 17%), 15% (9%, 21%)

key_safety: Most common (>2%) adverse reactions: pruritus (5%), headache (4%), nausea (4%), vasodilatation (3%) and paresthesia (3%); anaphylaxis/anaphylactoid reactions were the most common serious reactions (2 of 1676 subjects)
target_moa: Following IV injection, gadofosveset binds reversibly to endogenous serum albumin, giving a longer vascular residence time and increasing magnetic resonance relaxivity, which shortens the T1 relaxation time of water protons and increases blood signal intensity (brightness)
modality: Small molecule gadolinium-based contrast agent (gadolinium GdDTPA chelate with a diphenylcyclohexylphosphate group), a radiopharmaceutical/imaging agent

boxed_warning.content: Nephrogenic Systemic Fibrosis (NSF): gadolinium-based contrast agents increase the risk for NSF in patients with acute or chronic severe renal insufficiency (GFR <30 mL/min/1.73m2) or acute renal insufficiency of any severity due to hepato-renal syndrome or in the perioperative liver transplantation period

advisory_committee.vote: Not presented to an Advisory Committee because the product is a member of the GBCA class and did not present unique safety concerns

summary.text: New molecular entity GBCA approved under section 505(b) following a complicated multi-cycle regulatory history (two prior approvable letters, 2004 and November 2005) that was resolved by a re-read of the two aortoiliac studies; approved as the first FDA-approved agent for MRA, with a 505(o) post-marketing NSF clinical trial requirement and a boxed warning for NSF

citations.quote: This New Drug Application (NDA) was submitted for gadofosveset trisodium injection (Vasovist), a new molecular entity within the class of products generally referred to as "gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCAs)."
This application has a complicated regulatory history.
Hence, Vasovist will be the first FDA-approved agent for magnetic resonance angiography (MRA).
Therefore, based on appropriate scientific data, FDA has determined that you are required, pursuant to section 505(o)(3) of the FDCA, to conduct the following clinical trial:

requirement.text: A clinical trial to collect clinical data sufficient to assess the magnitude of risk for the development of NSF with the product among patients with moderate (GFR <60 mL/min/1.73m2) to severe renal insufficiency (required under section 505(o)(3))

basis.text: Lack of persuasive diagnostic efficacy data; FDA noted the data did not provide conclusive evidence that Vasovist added value to MRA performed without Vasovist
